keyFindings.description: Decision records are lost under load, and A5 counts from Dispatch. A process holding no id for a session lists every project document (GET /projects/INFRA/artifacts: 2.1 s, 4.5 MB, 2,153 documents, growing one per session) inside the record's 5 s stop; the tester saw 13 of 31 records given up under about 22 sessions, and 13 of 15 of those sessions were on their first record. Since bd250c48 the record runs after the call returns, so nothing needs the 5 s bound. Fix: read the document by name (getProjectArtifact, 0.07 s; upload only on 404); let one record write run under the client's own keyed retries (one Idempotency-Key per write, so a late first attempt is replayed, not doubled) until it is written or the shutdown cut; give each record an id (the tool call id, or the ledger line's id for an unmarked write) the reader de-duplicates on; and have the session-file report count the advisor-gate-record entries and the unmarked entries' recordError, so a record still lost at shutdown shows in a count.

The stop is armed when a record is queued, not when its write starts: queued records share one budget and are told Dispatch did not answer when Dispatch never got them, and the write still starts with an aborted signal. Reproduced: three records, 3 s per docEdit, records 2 and 3 'did not answer within 5000 ms'. New in 2d7d78a4.

Two definitions of where the override comment may stand disagree on a line continuation: keepOverrideVisible writes at lineEnd past a continuation and overrideComment rejects it, so the read-back drops the comment and the agent is told AskGate removed the flag, the case the visible comment exists for (askgate.test.ts:2771). One fact from dispatchCommandHead should serve both.
Wording, Security[untrusted-input]: 'every word quoted, so nothing can run wherever it stands' is false (reproduced in bash inside a single-quoted value); safety rests on lineEnd.

Read-back: head.comment !== undefined can never be true, and sameArgv and the rebuttal-line clause follow from the text comparison; each survives deletion. Keep one check that states the rule, or test each clause.
Previous finding 8 partly: the 'record ran after the mint' assertion survives the record moved before the mint; and 'whose record fails' names the session entry.
A refusal caused by a failed entry write is still recorded as decision allow; only a mint refusal is rewritten.
Wording: 'they land in the order the gate made them' fails once a stop fires (Dispatch finishes a given-up keyed write while the next is sent).
Duplication: four copies of the timed-client line where one helper was, and DispatchSession declared twice.
Dead code: the rejection arm of queued.then(write, write); its comment credits it with :330-333's guarantee.
abandoned() maps an impossible 'timeout' to success; name Exclude<Cause,'timeout'> once (written five times) and throw on timeout.
The shutdown cut has two owners depending on whether the gate loaded; one bind-time handler should own the cut and its delay.
Stale wording: 'neither imports the other' (askgate-report.ts imports the reader), the per-call order, and cutRecords, which is gone.
The override surface computed twice with a fallback, kept-or-removed stored in the per-surface table; a tombstone comment where RULE_REFUSED was.
